- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; apply upward bias correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope after spike.
- Model consistently underestimates true price movements in early forecast windows (e.g., first 5–7 days of 30d forecast) — apply upward bias to early horizon.
- If sentiment shifts from neutral to bullish mid-forecast, model often fails to adjust — trigger re-calibration or add sentiment-weighted momentum factor.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if forecast is trending upward, true price often reverses after 10–15 days — cap upward momentum after 10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish spikes followed by bearish corrections, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast volatility after 3–5 bullish days.
